title: The average distance of spanning trees in terms of independence number
summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph with vertex set $V(G)$, and denote by $d_G(u,v)$ the distance from $u$ to $v$ in $G$, for any $u,v \in V(G)$. The average distance of an $n$-vertex connected graph $G$, denoted by $μ(G)$, is defined to be the average of all distances between all pairs of vertices in $G$, i.e., $μ(G) = \binom{n}{2}^{-1} \sum_{\{u,v\} \subset V(G)}d_G(u,v)$. The problem of finding a spanning tree of minimum average distance is known to be NP-hard, so establishing an upper bound for the minimum average distance among all spanning trees is of particular interest.
